coursework.en: Whether, when and how generative AI may be used is set by each instructor and stated in the syllabus; students must follow course and departmental policies. Directly copying output, passing off AI output (including reworded or paraphrased output) as your own, or exceeding the instructor's limits is an academic integrity violation. Some departments are stricter: Art and Archaeology bans AI text generation, drafting and editing in coursework unless an instructor grants a disclosed exception.
coursework.zh: 是否、何时及如何使用生成式 AI 由各课程教师决定并写入课程大纲；学生须遵守课程和院系规定。直接复制输出、把 AI 输出（包括改写或意译后的输出）当作自己的成果，或超出教师限定范围，均构成学术诚信违规。部分院系更严格：艺术与考古学系禁止在课程作业中用 AI 生成、起草或润色文字，除非教师书面准许并要求披露的例外。

exams.en: No university-wide AI permission applies to examinations. Undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots, when completing quizzes or examinations or any work for an academic requirement, and exceeding the instructor's parameters is a violation. Art and Archaeology prohibits AI text generation in final examinations.
exams.zh: 考试没有全校性的 AI 使用许可。本科生在完成测验、考试或任何学业要求的作业时，不得使用普林斯顿以外的辅导资源，包括 AI 辅导机器人；超出教师规定范围即属违规。艺术与考古学系禁止在期末考试中用 AI 生成文字。

disclosure.en: When an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite it, because AI is not a source. Failing to disclose, including AI used for rewording, paraphrasing or editing, is a scholarly integrity violation even in courses where AI is allowed. Instructors may supply a disclosure template; otherwise the University template asks which tool was used, for what purpose, and confirms records were kept.
disclosure.zh: 教师允许使用生成式 AI 时，学生必须进行披露，而不是把 AI 当作来源引用，因为 AI 不是来源。即使在允许 AI 的课程中，未披露（包括用 AI 改写、意译或润色）也属于学术诚信违规。教师可提供披露模板；否则可使用学校模板，说明所用工具、用途并确认保留了使用记录。

privacy_data.en: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy covers administrative and operational University information (student, financial, HR records), not information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. For that information, Internal or Confidential data may only go into University-licensed AI tools, never into public AI tools, and Restricted data must not be used with any AI tool. Research and teaching data follow their own rules.
privacy_data.zh: 普林斯顿《生成式 AI 工具使用政策》适用于学校行政与运营信息（学生、财务、人事记录），不包括用于研究、学术或教学的信息。对这类信息，内部或机密数据只能输入学校许可的 AI 工具，不得输入公共 AI 工具；受限数据不得用于任何 AI 工具。研究和教学数据另有规定。

approved_tools.en: OIT lists Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Adobe Creative Cloud image generation for faculty, students and staff without a request. Other tools (Claude/Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Gemini Workspace+, Gemini Notebook, the AI Sandbox) are for faculty and those they sponsor, Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium is faculty-only, and Zoom AI is a faculty/staff pilot; these require a request and the directory marks a cost. Tools are approved for Public, Internal and Confidential data, not Restricted. Access is not permission to use a tool in a course.
approved_tools.zh: OIT 目录列出 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat 和 Adobe Creative Cloud 图像生成，教师、学生和员工无需申请即可使用。其他工具（Claude/Claude Code、GitHub Copilot、Gemini Workspace+、Gemini Notebook、AI Sandbox）面向教师及其担保人员，Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium 仅限教师，Zoom AI 为教职员工试点；这些需申请，目录标注涉及费用。工具获准处理公开、内部和机密数据，不含受限数据。能使用工具不等于课程允许使用。

do.zh: 获准使用 AI 时须披露（而非引用），包括用于改写、意译或润色的情况，并保留使用记录。

do.en: Use University-licensed tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with your Princeton login when working with non-public information.
do.zh: 处理非公开信息时，使用学校许可的工具（如用普林斯顿账号登录的 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat）。

dont.en: Do not copy AI output or submit reworded AI text as your own, and do not exceed what your instructor allows.
dont.zh: 不要复制 AI 输出或把改写后的 AI 文字当作自己的成果提交，也不要超出教师允许的范围。

dont.en: Undergraduates: do not use AI tutoring bots or other non-Princeton tutoring when completing homework, problem sets, quizzes or exams.
dont.zh: 本科生：完成作业、习题、测验或考试时，不要使用 AI 辅导机器人或其他非普林斯顿辅导资源。

dont.en: Do not put Restricted data into any AI tool, or non-public Princeton data into public AI tools.
dont.zh: 不要把受限数据输入任何 AI 工具，也不要把非公开的普林斯顿数据输入公共 AI 工具。

CL-001.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4) states that generative AI is not a source; where an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge it. Disclosure of permitted use is therefore required, not merely recommended, while whether AI may be used at all is set by the course or department. Scholarly Integrity guidance says failure to disclose, even in a course where AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation, and offers a disclosure template.

evidence.quote: Generative AI is not a source as defined in this provision because its output is not created by a person. If generative AI is permitted by the instructor, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge the use, since it is an algorithm rather than a source.
evidence.location: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 178-178 of captured page text

evidence.quote: All the tenets of scholarly integrity apply to use of generative AI: students must not pass off any output by generative AI as their own, and so a failure of disclosure, even in a course where generative AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation.
evidence.location: How to disclose generative AI; lines 86-86 of captured page text

CL-002.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities states that students must adhere to course and departmental generative AI policies, and that inappropriate uses on work submitted for an academic requirement - directly copying output, representing AI output as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing it), exceeding the instructor's parameters, or failing to disclose use (including use for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) - constitute academic integrity violations.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for adhering to course and departmental policies regarding the use of generative AI. Inappropriate uses of generative AI on any work submitted to fulfill an academic requirement, such as directly copying the output, representing output generated by or derived from generative AI as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing output from generative AI and representing it as their own), exceeding the parameters of use specified by the instructor, or failing to disclose its use (including the use of generative AI for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) constitute violations of academic integrity.
evidence.location: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 143-143 of captured page text

CL-003.text: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy (last updated August 2026) governs Princeton administrative and operational information, including student, financial and HR information; it expressly excludes information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. Under it, only University-licensed generative AI tools should be used with University Information classified as Internal or Confidential, publicly available generative AI tools may not be used with such information, and even University-licensed tools should not be used with Restricted information. It is not a blanket rule covering all student coursework or research data.

evidence.quote: The purpose of this policy is to manage the use of Princeton University administrative and operational information with generative AI tools.
evidence.location: Purpose; lines 82-82 of captured page text

evidence.quote: For the purposes of this policy, University Information does not include information used for research, academic or instructional purposes.
evidence.location: Scope; lines 90-90 of captured page text

evidence.quote: University-licensed generative AI tools should be used with Princeton Information classified as Internal or Confidential under the University’s Information Security Policy
evidence.location: Policy; lines 190-190 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The use of publicly available generative AI tools in conjunction with such Princeton Information is not permitted by the University. University-licensed generative AI tools should not be used with Princeton Information classified as Restricted.
evidence.location: Policy; lines 100-100 of captured page text

CL-004.text: Princeton's Office of the Dean of the College requires faculty to set clear expectations for whether, when and how generative AI can be used and to state them in the course syllabus; all students are expected to disclose their generative AI use and not pass off AI-generated content as their own, and faculty may provide their own disclosure template or use the standard one.

evidence.quote: Faculty must set clear expectations for whether, when, and how generative AI can be used and state those expectations in the course syllabus. Work created with the assistance of AI tools should never be a proxy for original work. All students are expected to abide by scholarly integrity expectations for appropriate generative AI use, which include disclosing their use of generative AI and not passing off AI-generated content as their own work.
evidence.location: Students and Generative AI; lines 212-212 of captured page text

CL-005.text: Princeton's McGraw Center for Teaching and Learning recommends against using AI detection tools to determine whether students have violated an instructor's AI policy. This is teaching guidance, not a disciplinary evidence rule.

evidence.quote: We recommend against using AI detection tools to determine if students have violated your AI policy.

CL-007.text: Princeton's Dean of the College stated in the Fall 2023 memo that the decision to allow, limit or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work remains with the faculty. This is consistent with current course-procedure guidance requiring faculty to state their expectations in the syllabus; the 2023 memo is historical context rather than the current governing text.

evidence.quote: First and foremost, the decision to allow, limit, or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work will remain our faculty’s. Faculty members have the discretion to set their own generative AI policy for their courses.

draft-claim-princeton-ai-tutoring-bots.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4.5), as quoted by Scholarly Integrity, provides that undergraduates may use only Princeton-authorized academic support: when completing any work to fulfil an academic requirement (homework, problem sets, quizzes or examinations), undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots. This applies to work done for academic requirements; it is not a ban on all AI-assisted study.

evidence.quote: When completing any work to fulfill an academic requirement (such as homework assignments, problem sets, quizzes or examinations of any kind), undergraduate students may not make use of any non-Princeton tutoring resources, including paid or unpaid tutors, independent tutoring services, or AI tutoring bots.

draft-claim-princeton-art-archaeology-in.text: Princeton's Department of Art and Archaeology prohibits using AI as a text-generation tool in coursework, final examinations and independent projects: students may not submit AI-generated text, use AI-generated text as a draft they then modify or paraphrase, or use generative AI to edit and revise their work. Instructors may grant exceptions for a course assignment with written disclosure, but exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or senior thesis. This department rule is stricter than general course-by-course permission.

evidence.quote: As a result, the Department of Art & Archaeology explicitly prohibits the use of AI as a text-generation tool in the writing of coursework, final examinations, and independent projects alike.
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text

evidence.quote: A student may not rely on AI-generated text as a rough or partial draft, which they then modify or paraphrase before submitting it as their own work; likewise, a student may not use generative AI in editing and revising their work.
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text

evidence.quote: That said, an instructor may wish to grant exceptions for AI use in a course assignment as long as the student strictly follows the instructor’s guidelines and discloses the specific use in writing. Exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or the senior thesis.
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 511-511 of captured page text
